issues.display_title: Issue #446: Prevent Zero UUIDs in Notification Inserts
issues.main_description_html:
RESULT 14/08/26

? Implementation: Prevent Zero UUIDs in Notification Inserts

Root Cause

The notification models use uuid.UUID primary-key fields. Their create paths constructed model structs without setting ID. GORM serialized the Go zero value into the insert, preventing database defaults from generating UUIDs and causing duplicate primary-key errors.

Changes

  • Added newPushNotification with ID: uuid.New() for mobile Expo-token rows.
  • Added newWebNotification with ID: uuid.New() for web-token rows.
  • Updated TokenNotification create paths to use those initialized models.
  • Added newNotification with ID: uuid.New() for records created by PushNotification.
  • Preserved token lookup/update behavior and notification payload fields.
  • Added regression tests proving all three constructors return non-zero UUIDs.

Audit Result

  • Audited all typed GORM Create calls under src against UUID-primary-key models.
  • The three notification paths above were the affected paths.
  • Other typed UUID creates explicitly assign IDs.
  • Map and raw-SQL inserts that omit id do not send a zero UUID and remain database-default-dependent; they were outside this defect.

Files

  • src/Action/V1/Notifications/TokenNotification.go
  • src/Action/V1/Notifications/TokenNotification_test.go
  • src/Action/V1/Notifications/PushNotification.go
  • src/Action/V1/Notifications/PushNotification_test.go

Verification

go test ./src/Action/V1/Notifications -count=1 -timeout=60s

Git

  • Token registration fix: edbb108
  • Notification record fix: 51b1160

Problem

GORM inserts the zero value of a uuid.UUID primary-key field when a model struct is created without assigning its ID. The database UUID default is not used because the id column is explicitly included as 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000.

This affected notification token registration and notification creation:

  • Mobile push tokens in push_notification.
  • Web push tokens in notifications_web.
  • Notification records created by PushNotification in notifications.

The first zero-UUID insert could succeed; later inserts then failed with a duplicate primary-key violation.

Scope

  • Generate a non-zero UUID before every typed GORM create in the affected notification flows.
  • Cover mobile tokens, web tokens, and notification records.
  • Add focused regression tests for all three constructors.
  • Audit other typed GORM creates using UUID primary keys for the same defect.
  • Do not migrate or clean existing database rows.

Acceptance Criteria

  • New mobile push-token rows never use the zero UUID.
  • New web push-token rows never use the zero UUID.
  • New notification rows from PushNotification never use the zero UUID.
  • Existing update behavior remains unchanged.
  • No other typed GORM UUID create lacking an ID remains in src.
  • Notification tests pass.

QA Test Summary - 14 Aug 2026 (Retest)

Verdict: PASSED

The prior QA finding was invalid: it inspected the stale local qa-testing branch (093cbca) rather than the current origin/development implementation (a997685), which includes developer commits edbb108 and 51b1160. The issue has no developer comments beyond its description.

RESULT 14/08/26

✅ Implementation: Centralize JSON Map Decoding

Changes

  • Added ElasticSearch.DecodeJSONMap(json.RawMessage) as the single JSON-to-map decoder.
  • Replaced local Jsonb.ToMap calls in Elasticsearch user, post, and comment helpers.
  • Removed duplicate, unused Jsonb declarations from Elasticsearch bookmark and score-timeline cronjob packages.
  • Preserved direct json.Unmarshal behavior without validation, fallback values, logging, or new dependencies.
  • Added a table-driven unit test for valid object, invalid JSON, and null input.

Files

  • src/Utils/ElasticSearch/ElasticSearch.go
  • src/Utils/ElasticSearch/json_test.go
  • src/Utils/ElasticSearch/ElasticUsers/ElasticUsers.go
  • src/Utils/ElasticSearch/ElasticPost/ElasticPost.go
  • src/Utils/ElasticSearch/ElasticComment/ElasticComment.go
  • src/Utils/ElasticSearch/ElasticBookmark/ElasticBookmark.go
  • src/Action/V1/Cronjob/UpdateScoreTimeline.go

Verification

go test ./...
git diff --check
Invoke-WebRequest -UseBasicParsing http://127.0.0.1:9999/
Invoke-RestMethod http://127.0.0.1:9999/check-connection

Results:

  • Focused decoder test passes.
  • All repository tests pass.
  • Diff whitespace validation passes; Git reports only existing line-ending warnings.
  • API root returns HTTP 200 and API Running Well!.
  • Health response reports status: ok; Elasticsearch, database, Redis, RabbitMQ, and MinIO are up.

Git

a997685

Problem

Six packages declared the same local Jsonb wrapper and ToMap method. Every implementation only unmarshaled json.RawMessage into map[string]interface{}. Maintaining identical copies adds noise and allows behavior to drift.

Scope

  • Add one shared JSON-map decoder in src/Utils/ElasticSearch.
  • Replace duplicated callers in Elasticsearch user, post, and comment helpers.
  • Remove unused duplicate declarations from Elasticsearch bookmark and cronjob packages.
  • Preserve JSON decoding results and errors.
  • Test valid object, invalid JSON, and null behavior.
  • Do not change Elasticsearch connections, query behavior, API responses, or other redundant functions.
  • Do not commit or push changes.

Acceptance Criteria

  • One shared DecodeJSONMap implementation exists.
  • No local Jsonb.ToMap implementation remains in affected packages.
  • Existing callers use the shared decoder.
  • Valid JSON objects decode to the same map.
  • Invalid JSON returns an error.
  • JSON null returns a nil map without an error.
  • go test ./... succeeds.
  • Live API root and dependency health endpoints succeed.
  • git diff --check succeeds.

  • Do not change worker code, endpoint contracts, or domain behavior.
  • Do not commit or push changes.

RESULT 14/08/26

✅ Implementation: Centralize Base64 JSON Decoding

Changes

  • Added table-driven tests for valid, empty, malformed Base64, and malformed JSON input.

Git

Problem

Actions and Redis utilities repeatedly decode Base64 strings, unmarshal the decoded JSON, and ignore both errors. The same two-step behavior appears nineteen times.

Scope

  • Add one global Functions.DecodeBase64JSON helper.
  • Preserve the existing best-effort behavior: decode and unmarshal errors are ignored without returning an API error.
  • Replace all matching non-worker call sites.
  • Test valid, empty, malformed Base64, and malformed JSON input.
  • Do not change workers, endpoint responses, Redis keys, or business rules.
  • Do not commit or push changes.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Valid Base64 JSON populates the supplied target.
  • Empty, fully invalid Base64, or malformed JSON input preserves the target's zero value.
  • All nineteen matching call sites use Functions.DecodeBase64JSON.
  • No matching inline block that ignores both decode and unmarshal errors remains outside workers.
  • Focused tests and go test ./... succeed.
  • git diff --check succeeds.

Excluded Scope

  • Redis.go keeps one decode block that unmarshals only when Base64 decoding succeeds; replacing it would change behavior for partial decode results.
